slides.texte_overlay:
Things that make you
surprisingly easy to talk to
Turning towards people when they speak. Shoulders, feet and face pointed at them. Your body says "I'm listening" before you've said a single word.
Repeating a key word they used. "Wait, you quit your job to sail?" Picking up their words shows you're following and invites them to tell you more.
Sharing a small embarrassing story. "I once called my boss mum." A little self-mockery tells people you're relaxed, and it makes them relax and open up too.
Never checking your phone mid-conversation. Not even a glance at a notification. Full attention is rare today, and people feel it and appreciate it straight away.
Always having a fresh topic. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a curious mind makes every conversation easy to start and easy to keep going.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A curious mind makes conversations easy to start and to keep going.

slides.texte_overlay: Laughing at their jokes when they're actually funny. A real laugh is a gift. People love talking to someone who genuinely enjoys what they say, and they come back for more.
Being honest when you don't understand. "I'm lost, explain that to me." Genuine interest is far more comfortable to be around than someone pretending.
